note: Iceland's tax and contribution rules, 2015-2025, kept by hand. Rates are staðgreiðsla (state plus the national average municipal tax); thresholds are monthly, in that year's krónur. Where a rule changed mid-year the annual value is the average by months and both are given.

sources.income_tax: Skatturinn, Helstu tölur og prósentur, 2016-2025 (skatturinn.is/einstaklingar/helstutolur/<year>/); 2015: Skatturinn, Staðgreiðsla 2015
sources.employer_pension: SA-ASÍ agreement of 21 January 2016: employer contribution 8% rising to 8.5% (1 July 2016), 10% (1 July 2017), 11.5% (1 July 2018)
sources.inheritance_floor: 1.5 m kr. 2011-2020 and 5 m in 2021 (lög 14/2004 as amended; Alþingi 5/151); indexed to the CPI from 2022: 2022-2023 estimated from the CPI, 2024-2025 Skatturinn

inheritance_floor._note: 1.5 m kr. 2011-2020 and 5 m in 2021 (lög 14/2004 as amended; Alþingi 5/151); indexed to the CPI from 2022: 2022-2023 estimated from the CPI, 2024-2025 Skatturinn

crisis_support_pct_gdp._note: COVID measures above the line: about 3% of GDP (IMF 2021 Article IV, for 2020); 2021 EST. Automatic stabilisers come from the model itself.

one_offs.2016: stability contributions from the old banks' estates (+12.7% of GDP balance): excluded when comparing the budget

job_retention._note: EST: share of the tourism jobs a collapse would end that hlutabætur (partial unemployment benefit with reduced hours) kept on the payroll. Its cost is inside crisis_support_pct_gdp.
